clue.text: West African's ready in school indeed after dropping round

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it fall away, so a piece is removed from the build

blocks.note: a coed is a coeducational school
I is an old spelling of aye, yes or indeed
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A West African pupil is all set for school.
explanation.walkthrough: Take COED plus I and drop the O to leave CEDI. 'Ready' is slang for cash, so 'West African's ready' is that region's money.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedi is the currency of Ghana, and ready money is cash.

clue.text: Mostly difficult to decipher English poet

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: crabbed handwriting is cramped and hard to read

explanation.surface: Remarks that an English poet's verse is largely obscure.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the D from CRABBED.
explanation.definitionFit: George Crabbe was an English poet of the late 1700s, author of The Borough.

clue.text: Court pieces excited one not wanting to devolve more power

definitions.text: one not wanting to devolve more power

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bits of a court case stir up a campaigner against handing over power.
explanation.definitionFit: A Eurosceptic opposes giving more powers to the European Union, resisting the transfer of authority away from the nation.

clue.text: Heads to roll, police lack genetic data carrier

indicators.note: heads rolling means leaders are cut off, so first letters go

blocks.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department
want means lack

explanation.surface: A police data scandal means senior officers must go.
explanation.walkthrough: Behead both CID and WANT. The CID is the British detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: An idant is an old biological term for a chromosome, which carries genetic information.

clue.text: Ill with a stab wound from weapon in Rome

indicators.note: wound read as the past tense of wind: the letters are twisted round into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a stab taken as written; with just joins it on

explanation.surface: Someone is laid low by a stab wound inflicted by an ancient Roman weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like the noun injury, but it is the verb wind, twisting the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballista was a Roman siege engine that hurled stones or bolts, so it is a weapon used in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Count that's supporting polls in by-election and suchlike

indicators.note: a poll is a head, so the heads of these words are taken
in a down answer, supporting means placed underneath the other piece

blocks.note: first letters of by-election, and, suchlike
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Counting polling figures in by-elections and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb about tallying votes, but it is a jazz title. 'Poll' is an old word for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie was an American jazz bandleader whose stage name included the title Count.

clue.text: Boss has institution for publicity in part of Ireland

indicators.note: has ... for means one thing is put in place of another

blocks.note: a leader is a boss
inst. abbreviates institution
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A boss uses an institution for publicity somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: In LEADER, swap AD for INST; 'for' signals the swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Leinster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, in the east.

clue.text: Article about ball-game again

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: an item is an article, as in a newspaper
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A news piece about a ball game is being run once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Iterum is Latin for once more, used in English for a repeat occurrence.

clue.text: Flipping hookers wrecked game plan

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the letters run backwards
wrecked means smashed, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: tarts is slang for prostitutes, hookers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Annoyed rugby hookers ruined the game plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British expletive and 'hookers' as rugby forwards; one is a reversal signal, the other prostitutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or trick for gaining an advantage, a cunning plan.

clue.text: Stupid people to get second estimate

blocks.note: asses are fools
S abbreviates second

explanation.surface: Fools seeking a second opinion on a valuation.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge the value or amount of something, which is to estimate it.

clue.text: Manage Yorkshire area land

blocks.note: to run a business is to manage it
the Yorkshire Dales are a hilly region of northern England

explanation.surface: An instruction to look after a stretch of Yorkshire farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are a national park area of valleys in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rundale is an old Irish and Scottish system of holding land in scattered strips, so rundales are parcels of land.

clue.text: Trips emerge disastrously for fisherman

indicators.note: disastrously suggests things going badly wrong, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fishing trips that turn out badly for the man at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The fisherman comes from Crabbe's poem The Borough, answer to 1 down, and Britten's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Grimes is the brutal fisherman in Crabbe's poem and Britten's opera of the same name.

clue.text: Cordial about club twills

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: cassis is a blackcurrant cordial or liqueur
a mere is a Maori war club

explanation.surface: A golf or social club serving fruit cordial to members in tweeds and twills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a golf club or society, but here it is a short Maori war club of stone or greenstone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassimere is a twilled woollen cloth, so cassimeres are kinds of twill fabric.

clue.text: Curses keeping party member well back for Europeans

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters from right to left
keeping means holding inside, so the other letters sit within

blocks.note: to curse in the old sense is to put under a ban
a member of the party is in it
so, as in 'so, what next?', is a filler like well

explanation.surface: Swearing at a well-backed party member, presumably in European politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well back' reads as well-supported, but 'back' reverses both party member and well together before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosnians are people from Bosnia, a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Desire for one way to meet Charles

blocks.note: a street is a way or road
Car. abbreviates Carolus, Latin for Charles

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a way to meet a man called Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' looks like longing, but it is the name in Tennessee Williams's play A Streetcar Named Desire; 'for one' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire is the streetcar named in the title of Tennessee Williams's play, so it is an example of a tram.

clue.text: Boarding head right away gives a tip

indicators.note: away means sent off, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: to lag pipes is to cover them with insulating boards or felt
napper is British slang for the head
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A boarding-school head goes off and leaves a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the R from NAPPER. 'Napper' is old British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagniappe is a small bonus or gratuity given in addition, in American usage, so a tip.

clue.text: Instruments not loud? Get different ones

indicators.note: not tells us to go without something, so that piece is taken away

blocks.note: flutes are woodwind instruments
f is forte, the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: Asking for quieter instruments, the answer is to swap them for others.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F from FLUTES. The definition refers back to 'Instruments': the answer is a different set of instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Lutes are plucked string instruments, so they are other instruments than the flutes in the wordplay.

clue.text: Off-white in spring returning? Not so

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is taken right to left
not says those letters are absent from the final result

blocks.note: a spring is the source of a stream
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether off-white clothes will come back into fashion in spring, and being told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' looks like a reply to the question, but it orders the removal of SO from the reversed spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow shade of unbleached linen, a type of off-white.

clue.text: Action around English river in Indian vessels

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: pas is a step or movement in dance, an action
the Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: Activity on an English river involving boats from India.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river on the Devon and Cornwall border; PAS is the dance-step word.
explanation.definitionFit: A patamar is a lateen-rigged sailing boat used on the west coast of India.

clue.text: Youngster put his shirt on horse? Ends with the bookmaker!

indicators.note: ends points to the final letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
a nag is a horse, usually an old one
the last letters of the and bookmaker

explanation.surface: A young gambler bets everything on a horse and the bookie wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put his shirt on' is the idiom for betting everything; here the shirt is literally placed before the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a person aged thirteen to nineteen, a youngster.

clue.text: Vehicle hit them, according to reports

indicators.note: reports are things heard, so the sound of the phrase is what counts

blocks.note: to tan someone is to beat them; 'em is them

explanation.surface: News reports of a vehicle that struck people.
explanation.walkthrough: To tan someone's hide is British slang for to thrash them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tandem is a bicycle for two riders, one behind the other, so a vehicle.

clue.text: Not entirely agreeable covering a do on ships

indicators.note: not entirely means not the whole thing, so the end is cut off
covering means going over and round, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: nice means agreeable
taken as written
ut is the old name for the note do in sol-fa

explanation.surface: A not wholly pleasant party held on board ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party, but it is the first note of the scale, once called ut.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautic is a rare form of nautical, meaning relating to ships and sailing.

clue.text: Spurs for example start on goal with Son finishing

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
first letter of goal
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, nicknamed Spurs, start with a goal and their player Son finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur football club, and Son Heung-min was their striker; here Spurs is the verb 'urges on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge them forward, so eggs means spurs as a verb.

clue.text: Without date and without giving property title to a Scot

blocks.note: s.a. abbreviates sine anno, without date
sine is Latin for without

explanation.surface: Lacking a date and anything else, a Scot is handed a deed to property.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a sasine is the act of giving possession of feudal property, or the deed recording it.

clue.text: One point is vertical at sea

blocks.note: a means one
a peak is a pointed top

explanation.surface: A navigational remark that a single point stands upright out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Apeak is a nautical term for an anchor or oar held vertically, so it means vertical in a sailing context.

clue.text: Out of place, go off last part of Greek drama

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so those letters are lifted away

blocks.note: Pl. abbreviates place in addresses
a bomb goes off when it explodes

explanation.surface: A misplaced bomb goes off in the closing act of a Greek tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The exode is the final scene or closing section of an ancient Greek play, after the last choral song.

clue.text: Girl one's seen in black

indicators.note: seen in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: jet black is a deep black
an means one

explanation.surface: A girl is spotted dressed in black.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is a female first name, so it is a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Fellow with a wife meets a young girl briefly? They can't be trusted

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written
ux. abbreviates Latin uxor, wife
taken as written
a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A married man who meets a young girl on the side is not to be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: UX for wife comes from legal Latin uxor. The definition fits the surface's cheating husband but really means false friends in language.
explanation.definitionFit: Faux amis are false friends: words in two languages that look alike but differ in meaning, so they mislead.

clue.text: Long forgotten, caught child on tape recorder

indicators.note: what is forgotten is left out, so that letter goes
caught as in caught up or tangled, so the letters are jumbled together

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for long
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old recording of a child, long forgotten, has turned up on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the L from CHILD ON TAPE and rearrange the rest. 'Tape' is part of the fodder, so the definition is just 'recorder'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dictaphone is a trademarked machine for recording speech for later typing, a kind of recorder.

clue.text: Resort village in Greece to get new diggers

blocks.note: a spa is a health resort
a deme is a township or district of ancient Attica
N abbreviates new

explanation.surface: A Greek resort village takes on fresh labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Spademen are workers who dig with spades, so they are diggers.

clue.text: Noble earl behind border district

indicators.note: behind says this piece trails after the next one in the answer

blocks.note: the Marches are the borderlands, especially between England and Wales
E abbreviates earl

explanation.surface: An aristocrat on the frontier, with an earl lurking at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Welsh Marches are the English counties along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchese is an Italian marquis, a nobleman of high rank.

clue.text: Card digits spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means we go by how the word is said, not spelt

blocks.note: toes are the digits of the foot

explanation.surface: A playing card with numbers being talked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a playing card, but it is the verb meaning to comb out wool.
explanation.definitionFit: To tose or toze is an old word meaning to tease or card wool, combing out its fibres.
